instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Use the Right Vocabulary
cards.instruction: Perform belonging by using official language confidently, adjusting each term whenever someone reveals what it actually means.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've reconciled the invoices, just like you: all the blue ones in one drawer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was clearing my desk. Reconcile means match them to the purchase orders.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Blue batch ready for reconciliation. These totals look like estimates.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They are. Those aren't invoices; they're quotes for work we haven't ordered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Quotes pending orders, then. I'll relabel the drawer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Carried unanimously! I'll put the minutes in the cupboard, the way you did.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Those were old minutes. Carried means the vote passed; we both have to vote first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. Motion awaiting carriage. I'm in favor; you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm against. And it's 'carried,' not 'carriage.'

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: One for, one against: not carried. I'll enter the split in the minutes.

cards.title: More Official Than You
cards.instruction: Turn every suggestion into a contest over whose method, title, precedent, or paperwork is more legitimate.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stamped our picnic rota like you stamped yours. Mine's official now, so we'll use it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My stamp says VOID. I made a mistake. Let's use this clean copy.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, voided. Mine records the mistake; your clean copy has no audit trail.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then attach your voided sheet behind the rota people can actually read.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: In front, please. The corrected rota follows my original decision.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I bowed when you did, but lower. As deputy chair I should set the ceremonial standard.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was picking up my programme. Just wave to the founder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, programmes first. My bow still respects the original ceremony.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The founder's waving us over for a photograph.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll bow beside him for the photograph. That will give next year's deputy chair an official reference.

cards.title: A Valuable Safeguard
cards.instruction: Treat every delay, restriction, and extra step as evidence that the system is becoming safer and more thorough.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I stretched red ribbon across every doorway, like yours at the front. A much safer climbing centre.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's for the mayor to cut at the opening. People need those doors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Precisely, controlled openings. We can check each doorway before we cut the ribbon.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The mayor's here for five minutes. She can only do the front.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. We'll keep the others closed until someone can inspect them properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've drawn boxes round every signature like you did. Nobody goes on the trip until all the boxes are checked.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was marking the signatures we couldn't read. Those others are fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, a complete legibility check. Best have another teacher look before we let anyone board.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: June can read them, but she's supervising the children on the bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll wait for her to finish. I wouldn't pull her away from a safety job.

cards.title: Warmly Enforced
cards.instruction: Remain kind and welcoming while enforcing increasingly restrictive rules without exception.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my shoes outside, same as you. Lovely to have you staying, but shoes must remain on the step.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are muddy. Yours are dry; you can bring them in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, keep the mud outside. I'll lend you slippers, but those stay indoors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll clean my shoes before my train. Could I use your sink?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Happily—I'll bring a bowl outside. Leave the slippers here, please; they stay indoors.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I copied your crossed arms at the pool door. Welcome back! Nobody through until the whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I crossed them because I'm cold. The pool's open.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Come and warm up in reception; we'll wait for the whistle there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The lifeguard's just whistled for everyone to leave the water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's keep their way clear. There's a lovely seat for you at the far end of reception.

cards.title: There Is a Process
cards.instruction: Treat every favor, feeling, and urgent need as a request requiring terms, documentation, review, and approval.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You numbered the place cards, so I've numbered the tissues. Before I issue yours, which table are you crying about?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: None. I'm crying because my daughter is getting married.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, bride's family. I'll put you under table one; can you confirm that's your seat?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not sitting down. I'm walking her down the aisle.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sign for a tissue now and keep it with you. We can settle the table number afterward.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've written you a ticket like the baker gave you. Now, how long do you need my umbrella?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He gave me a receipt. I just need the umbrella till I reach the bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, a receipt for the loan. Write your return time where he put the price.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm asking a friend for a favor, and my bus is coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write 'no charge,' then. I'll approve it while you sign.
